extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: SWE-Gym is the first environment for training software engineering (SWE) agents. It contains 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language. The dataset is sourced from pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories, with pre-configured executable environments and expert-validated test cases. SWE-Gym is used to train language model based SWE agents and verifiers, enabling inference-time scaling.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.citeAs: Pan, J., Wang, X., Neubig, G., Jaitly, N., Ji, H., Suhr, A., & Zhang, Y. (2025). Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym. Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, Vancouver, Canada. PMLR 267.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: SWE-Gym was constructed by identifying Python repositories using SEART GitHub search, filtering for repositories created before July 1, 2022 with more than 500 stars, at least 300 lines of code, more than 500 pull requests, and 100 contributors. Task instances were extracted from GitHub pull requests using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script. Executable environments were manually configured for 11 repositories, and instances were validated using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script. The process required approximately 200 human annotation hours and 10,000 CPU core hours.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Instances that failed the executable environment setup and validation process were filtered out. Out of 64,689 raw task instances, only 2,438 passed validation and were included in the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: GitHub pull requests and issues from 358 Python repositories, collected via SEART GitHub search. The raw dataset (SWE-Gym Raw) contains 64,689 task instances spanning 358 Python repositories, each corresponding to a GitHub issue including the natural language description, a snapshot of the repository, and a set of unit tests.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Repositories created before July 1, 2022 were included. The exact end date of the collection process is not explicitly stated.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Instances were versioned by associating them with their respective version numbers and setting up environments version-by-version. Dependencies were manually configured for each task instance using relevant configuration files (e.g., requirements.txt), CI scripts, or documentation from the repository snapshot at the time of issue creation. A subset of 230 tasks (SWE-Gym Lite) was identified following the SWE-Bench Lite filtering pipeline, excluding tasks requiring editing more than one file, tasks with poorly described problem statements, those with excessively complex ground-truth code diffs, and tests focused on error message validation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Raw instances from 358 repositories were filtered to 11 repositories with numerous instances for which executable environments were semi-manually created. Instances were validated using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script to ensure the gold patch passes more unit tests than the original code. Failed instances were filtered out, resulting in 2,438 validated instances. Pre-built Docker images were created for each instance for reproducibility.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Executable environments were manually configured by a subset of the authors for each task instance. The gold patches (human-submitted code diffs from GitHub pull requests) serve as ground truth. Unit tests from the original repositories serve as the evaluation signal. The annotation process required approximately 200 human annotation hours.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: SWE-Bench's instance extraction script and execution-based validation script; SEART GitHub search; Docker for pre-built images
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Instances were validated by checking that the gold patch (human-submitted code diff) passes more unit tests than the original code using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script. Instances failing this check were filtered out.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations were done by a subset of the authors (researchers at UC Berkeley, UIUC, CMU, and Apple).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SWE-Bench instance extraction script, SWE-Bench execution-based validation script, SEART GitHub search, SWE-Bench versioning script, OpenHands remote runtime, SGLang, torchtune, Unsloth
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: SWE-Gym, models, and agent trajectories are publicly released. Pre-built Docker images for each instance are released, totaling 6 TB. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy is described beyond the initial public release.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer productivity and accessibility across industries. As agents become more capable, they may impact software engineering jobs and require careful consideration around code ownership, licensing, and attribution. Similar techniques could potentially be misused to automate the creation of malicious code. The authors encourage future work to explore frameworks for responsible deployment of software engineering agents, including considerations around security, safety, and economic impacts.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The task distribution across repositories exhibits a long-tail pattern, with tasks associated with pandas comprising nearly one-third of the total, while tasks related to bokeh represent only one percent. The dataset is biased toward repositories with complex dependencies due to manual environment configuration. Repeated sampling for self-improvement introduces a bias toward easier tasks, as task success probability follows a long-tail distribution.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: SWE-Gym is limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories (11 for the main dataset), types of tasks, and programming languages (Python only). The dataset currently contains 2,438 instances, and performance improvements are currently limited by the compute budget for sampling rather than the number of tasks. The self-improvement results are modest, and more advanced policy optimization methods may be needed. The dataset covers only Python repositories.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training software engineering agents (LM fine-tuning via rejection sampling / supervised fine-tuning); Training verifier/reward models for inference-time scaling; Benchmarking and evaluating SWE agents; Research into self-improvement and reinforcement learning for code agents; Rapid prototyping using SWE-Gym Lite (230 instances); Future research in SWE agent development and automatic dataset synthesis using SWE-Gym Raw.
